Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 1:

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat Saba'

It is Makki.

﴿All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.﴾ That is: to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. It is also said: He created whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.

As for His saying: ﴿And to Him is the praise in the Hereafter.﴾ there are two opinions. The first: its meaning is that to Him belongs praise in the first and the last, as He said in another place. Regarding "the first and the last" there are two views: the first is that they are this world and the Hereafter, and the second is that they are the heavens and the earth.

The second opinion: His saying ﴿And to Him is the praise in the Hereafter﴾ refers to the mention of praise that came from the people of Paradise, and this is in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the last of their call will be: "All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ and in His saying: ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us all grief."﴾ and in His saying: ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us."﴾

As for His saying: ﴿And He is the Wise, the All-Aware.﴾ that is: Wise in His dominion, All-Aware of His creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 2:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿He knows what enters into the earth﴾, i.e., what enters into it of rain.

And His saying: ﴿and what comes out of it﴾, i.e., of plants. It is also said that what is meant is the dead, who enter (the earth) when they are buried, and come out when they are gathered (for resurrection).

And His saying: ﴿and what descends from the sky﴾, i.e., of rain, angels, decrees and judgments.

And His saying: ﴿and what ascends into it﴾, i.e., what rises up to it of angels, deeds, and accepted supplications.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Most Merciful, the Oft-Forgiving﴾. We have already explained this.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 3:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "The Hour will not come upon us."﴾ They said this as a denial of the Resurrection (al-ba'th).

And His saying: ﴿Say, "Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come upon you, the Knower of the unseen (ʿĀlim al-ghayb)."﴾ In it there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), and its meaning is: "Say: Yes, by my Lord, the Knower of the unseen, it will surely come upon you, the Hour." Hamzah recited "ʿallām al-ghayb."

And His saying: ﴿Not hidden from Him﴾ means: not concealed from Him. Yahya ibn Wathhab recited "lā yaghrub ʿanhu" with a ghayn (ghayn mu'jamah) and a ra'.

And His saying: ﴿The weight of an atom's (mithqal dharrah) in the heavens or on the earth﴾ means: the weight of an atom. ﴿Nor what is less than that or greater﴾ means: what is smaller than the atom, to the point that the intellect cannot grasp it, and what is greater, to the point that the intellect cannot grasp it. The meaning is that all of that is within His knowledge.

And His saying: ﴿Except that it is in a clear Book﴾ means: a manifest one.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿That He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ means: that He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds.

And His words: ﴿For them is forgiveness and a generous provision﴾ mean: the pleasant living.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 5:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them﴾. Its meaning: they were agitated and busied themselves in denying Our signs.

His saying: ﴿mu'ajizin﴾ means: opposing (mushaqqin), and it is said: competing (musabiqin), and it is said: escaping (fa'itin). It was also read as "mu'jizin", meaning: discouraging (muthabbitin). It was said: thinking that We cannot overcome them, so the meaning of mu'jizin is that they attributed incapacity (al-ajz) to Us.

His saying: ﴿For them is a painful punishment of wretched torment﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 6:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿And those who have been given knowledge see﴾. Some of them said: this refers to the believers among the People of the Book, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and others. The sound view is that the verse concerns those who believed in the Prophet from the people of Makkah and others, and it was (revealed) in Makkah, because the surah is Makkan, whereas ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his like only believed in Madinah.

His words: ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth﴾, meaning: it is from God, exalted is He.

His words: ﴿and guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy﴾, meaning: the Qur'an which God has sent down guides to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy, who is God, exalted is He.

God says: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Shall we direct you to a man who will inform you"﴾ — meaning: who will tell you (yunbi'ukum: yukhbirukum).

And His words: ﴿"When you are completely disintegrated"﴾ — meaning: when you are scattered in every way (tafriq) and cut into every kind of cutting; the meaning is: when the earth has consumed you and you have become decayed bones and dust, [he] will inform you, Muhammad, that "you are indeed in a new creation." They said this in the manner of denial and rejection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 8:

And His words: ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah, or is there madness in him?﴾ It is also read with the alif pointed with a fatha and with a kasra. As for the one who reads it with a kasra, it refers back to the reporting of the disbelievers, as if they had said: "Muhammad has invented a lie against Allah."

And His words: ﴿Or is there madness in him?﴾ its meaning: or is there madness in him, so that he does not know what he is saying.

As for the one who reads it with a fatha, there are two opinions. The first is that its meaning is: "Has he invented a lie against Allah?" meaning: he has not invented, and this is the beginning of speech from Allah, the Exalted. The poet said: (The heart has newly received news from their partisans... or has the heart returned from their songs to joy?)

And its meaning: it has newly received (news). The second opinion is that the meaning of His words ﴿Has he invented a lie against Allah?﴾ is: "Do you invent it as a fabrication against Allah, a lie?"

And His words: ﴿Nay, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are in punishment and far-off error.﴾ According to the first reading, with the kasra, this is the beginning of speech from Allah, the Exalted, as a refutation of them; and according to the second reading, it is connected to what preceded.

And His words: ﴿in punishment and far-off error﴾ meaning: lasting misery. This was mentioned by al-Suddi, who said: "in far-off error from the truth."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 9:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Have they not looked at what is before them and behind them of the heaven and the earth?﴾ The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: He only mentioned this because when a person leaves his house, he sees nothing but the heaven and the earth and what is in them. It is also said: He said this because the heaven and the earth encompass the creation, so it is as though one of them is before them and the other behind them, in the sense of encompassing.

And His words: ﴿If We wish, We shall cause the earth to swallow them up﴾, meaning: We shall make them disappear into the earth.

And His words: ﴿Or cause fragments of the heaven to fall upon them﴾, meaning: a part of the heaven. It is also said: a piece of the heaven.

And His words: ﴿Surely in that is a sign for every servant who turns back in repentance﴾, meaning: who returns to God, the Most High, with his heart. It is also said: "munib" means "mujib" (one who responds).

The poet said:

(He turned back to my words, so I became a watcher for him, with a repaying that is turning back and thanks.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 10:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And We bestowed upon Dawud (David) grace from Us﴾. Scholars differed concerning the grace (fadl) that Dawud was given. Some said it was prophethood (nubuwwah). Others said it was kingship (mulk). It is also said: judging with justice (al-qada' bil-'adl). It was said: beautiful voice (husn al-sawt). And it was said: the softening of iron for him, and all that he was given and singled out with.

As for His words: ﴿O mountains, echo the praises with him﴾, most of the people of tafsir hold that its meaning is: glorify (sabbihi) with him. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas and others. It is also said: return (irji'i) with him.

al-Hasan read: "awwibi ma'ahu" with a damma on the alif and a sukun on the waw, and it has the same meaning as the first.

In some tafsirs it is mentioned that when Dawud (peace be upon him) felt lethargy, Allah made him hear the glorification of the mountains as an encouragement to him.

As for His words: ﴿and the birds﴾, meaning: We commanded the birds to glorify with him.

As for His words: ﴿And We made iron soft for him﴾, Qatadah said: it was as if the iron was made pliable for him like dough, so he would make the coat of mail without fire or hammer.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 11:

And His words: ﴿Make complete coats of mail﴾ — that is, the full coats of mail. It is also said: the long ones that trail along the ground.

The poet said:

(And the most of them in coats of mail, complete ones... and the most incisive of them, when they thrust, in spear-points)

And His words: ﴿and be measured in the linking﴾ — that is, be balanced in the linking (al-sard). Its meaning: calibrate the rivets in the rings of the coats of mail, so that the rivet is not made thick and the ring is not made too narrow, whereby the ring would break; nor should the ring be made too wide and the rivet made thin, whereby it would become loose and unstable. This is the view of Mujahid, who said: "Be measured in the linking" means: perfect the weaving of the armour. Qatadah said: al-sard means the rivets in the rings. This is close to the view of Mujahid. They also recited:

(He perfected its linking and widened its rings)

He says: he widened them and perfected the ringing. It is said: a coat of mail is "masrudah" when its rings are riveted. It is also said: "be measured in the linking" means: keep to the middle course and the measure of need.

And His words: ﴿And work righteousness; indeed I am Seeing of what you do﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

In the story: Dawud, peace be upon him, used to make one coat of mail every day and sell it for six thousand dirhams. He would spend two thousand of them on himself and his family, and give four thousand in charity to the poor of the Children of Israel. In some tafsir works it is stated that he made a thousand coats of mail.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 12:

The words of God, Exalted is He: ﴿And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind; its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel].﴾ That is: We subjected the wind to Solomon.

And His words: ﴿its morning [journey] was a month's [travel] and its evening [journey] was a month's [travel]﴾ mean: the distance covered in its morning was a month's journey, and the distance covered in its evening was a month's journey. Its meaning is that he would travel the distance of two months in a single day. In the narration: he would travel from Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) to Istakhr a month's journey for a swift rider in the morning, and would rest there at midday, then in the evening travel a month's journey to Babylon, a month's journey for a swift rider. It was also said: he would take his midday meal in al-Ray and his evening meal in Samarqand. It was also said: he would take his midday meal in Sana'a and his evening meal in Babil, which is Iraq. And God knows best.

In the exegesis (tafsir) it is related that the wind would carry him and his armies, and it would not stir up dust, nor turn over a leaf on the ground, nor harm a bird in the sky.

And His words: ﴿And We caused a fount of molten copper to flow for him﴾. That is: We caused a fount of copper to flow for him.

In the exegesis it is related that God Almighty melted the copper for him, and it flowed for three days of every month like water.

And His words: ﴿And of the jinn were those who worked before him by the permission of his Lord﴾. That is: by the command of his Lord.

And His words: ﴿And whoever of them swerves from Our command﴾. That is: whoever of them deviates from Our command, so that he does not work for Solomon.

And His words: ﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾. That is: in the Hereafter. This is one of the two views. The other view is that there was (would be) with Solomon an angel standing with a whip of fire in his hand, so that whenever one of the devils disobeyed, he would strike him and burn him. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿We will make him taste the punishment of the Blaze﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 34, verse 13:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿They made for him whatever he wished of places of worship﴾, meaning: the masajid (mosques). It is also said: lofty buildings. In the narrative: he commanded them to build fortresses of rock, and in Yemen they built many wondrous fortresses, namely Sirwah, Marwah, Faltun, Hindah, Hunaydah, Ghumdan and others.

His saying: ﴿and statues﴾, meaning: images (ṣuwar). If someone says: Is not making images disliked? We say: that is in this sharia; it is possible that they were permissible in his sharia. Indeed ʿĪsā used to shape images from clay and blow into them, and God would make them birds. There is a difference of opinion concerning the images the devils made. One of the two views is that they were the images of beasts of prey and birds such as eagles and vultures, and what is similar to that.

The second view: that he commanded them to make images of the prophets, the ascetics and the worshippers, so that when the Children of Israel looked at them they would increase in worship.

His saying: ﴿and basins like reservoirs﴾, meaning: like watering-troughs; jifan is the plural of jafnah. In the narrative: each jafnah could seat a thousand people. Ḥassān recited poetry about the jafnah:

(For us are the bright basins gleaming in the forenoon, and our swords dripping with blood from valour.)

And they recited about the jābiyah:

(Like the jābiyah of the Iraqi shaykh overflowing.)

That is: filling up.

ʿUthmān ibn ʿAṭāʾ related from his father that he once saw one of these small bowls and said: "By God, blessing has gone from everything," and he recited His saying: ﴿and basins like reservoirs﴾.

In the narrative: Sulaymān (peace be upon him) had a table that could hold four hundred thousand people, and he himself would eat barley bread, while he fed his family and attendants khubz al-khushkār, and fed the poor darmak, which is pure bread.

His saying: ﴿and cooking-pots fixed firmly﴾, meaning: steadfast and elevated, and from this come the firm mountains (al-jibāl al-rawāsī). In the narrative, he would ascend to them by ladders.

His saying: ﴿Work, O family of Dawūd, in gratitude﴾. He said: the meaning is: "Give thanks to God with gratitude." It is also said: gratitude is the fear of God and acting in His obedience. It was said: "the family of Dawūd" is Dawūd himself; it is also said: Dawūd, Sulaymān and his household. In the narrative: when this was revealed to Dawūd, he said: "By God, there will never cease to be among us one who stands in prayer and fasts by night and day." So there was no day but that someone of the family of Dawūd was fasting in it, and no hour of the night but that someone of the family of Dawūd was standing in it. It is related that he divided the hours of the night among them, and he would stand for as long as God willed; when he wished to sleep, he would wake some of his family.

It is related that he said to Sulaymān (peace be upon him): "O my son, take care of the affairs of the day, meaning in worship, and I will take care of the affairs of the night." Sulaymān said: "I cannot." So he said: "Take care of the beginning of the day, and I will take care of the rest." It is also related that he said: "O Lord, how can I thank You, when my thanks to You is itself a blessing from You upon me?" He said: "Now you have thanked Me."

His saying: ﴿And few of My servants are grateful﴾: its meaning is apparent. The difference between "shākir" and "shakūr": the shakūr is one from whom gratitude recurs, and the shākir is one who gives thanks once. It is also said that the two are one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 14:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Then when We decreed death for him﴾, meaning: for Sulayman, death.

And His saying: ﴿Nothing indicated his death except a creature of the earth﴾. Some of the exegetes said: The jinn used to work for Sulayman, peace be upon him, in building the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis. Sulayman's death drew near while some of the work remained, so God took the soul of Sulayman while he was leaning on a staff, and they (the jinn) thought he was alive and kept striving at the work. Then the termite (al-ardah) ate the staff, and Sulayman, peace be upon him, fell down dead after a year, by which time they had finished the work. When they recognized his death, they dispersed, after they had continued at the work for a year after his death. Ibn 'Abbas said: The jinn then thanked the termite for that, so they bring it clay and water inside wood. Some of them also mentioned that Sulayman, peace be upon him, whenever he saw a tree growing, would ask it: "What is your name?" If it was for planting, it would tell him, and he would plant it; and if it was for medicine, he would write down its name. Once he prayed and saw a tree growing in his place of prayer, and he said to it: "What is your name?" It said: "Al-kharrub (carob)." He said: "For what did you grow?" It said: "For the ruin of this land." So he knew that his death had drawn near, and he asked God, Exalted, to conceal his death from the jinn. The people of exegesis said: The jinn used to claim that they know the unseen, so God, Exalted, commanded Sulayman to take a staff and lean upon it. It was said: He took it from that tree, and God, Exalted, took his soul while he was standing leaning on the staff, so the jinn kept looking at him and thinking he was alive, and they kept working until he fell after a year. God, Exalted, intended by this to make the jinn know that they do not know the unseen. It was also said: so that mankind would know that the jinn do not know the unseen, and they (the jinn) had made this appear doubtful to mankind. If it is said, according to the first interpretation: How could it be unclear to anyone whether he knows the unseen or does not? And if the matter of another was hidden from him, would the matter of himself not be hidden from him? The answer: The rebellious jinn had portrayed to the weak among the jinn that they know the unseen, and some coincidences would occur, so they used to think that they know the unseen, due to the predominance of ignorance. And according to some of them: their work was not in building the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis, for its completion had occurred years earlier; rather they were doing other works.

And His saying: ﴿His staff﴾, meaning: his staff. The minsa'ah (staff) is a staff in the Abyssinian language. It is also read as "minsa'atihi" with the hamzah silent, and it is what we have explained.

The poet said:

(When you lean on the minsa'ah from old age... then play and dalliance have distanced themselves from you)

It is said that both are in Arabic. It is also said: nasa'a al-ghanam means when one drives and herds the sheep, and it is said: nasa'a Allah fi ajalika means: He postponed it (your term).

And His saying: ﴿So when it fell, the jinn became evident﴾, meaning: the jinn became clear to mankind that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment, meaning: the toil and the long hardship. Al-Azhari mentioned this on this explanation. As for the earlier scholars, they said its meaning is: mankind became clear that the jinn, had they known the unseen, would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. The reading is thus in the Codex of Ibn Mas'ud, and Ibn 'Abbas also read it so. The third interpretation: that the meaning of the verse is: "the jinn became clear," meaning: the jinn came to know that, had they known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas in another narration: that Sulayman was not leaning on the staff; rather he was in a closed room, and God took him, and the termite ate the threshold of the door, so the door fell after a year, and his death became apparent to the jinn.

The more famous of the two accounts is the first. In the story: when Sulayman, peace be upon him, finished building the mosque, he sacrificed [twelve] thousand cows and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep, seeking nearness to God, Exalted, and fed them to the people. He had built it of stone and pitch, decorated the walls, and adorned the niche with jewels and rubies, and they made something wondrous. Then he stood upon the rock and said: "O God, You gave me this great dominion, and You subjected to me what You subjected. So inspire me to be grateful for Your blessing which You have bestowed upon me, do not let my heart swerve after You have guided me, and cause me to die as a Muslim, and join me with the righteous. O God, I ask You for five qualities for whoever enters this mosque to pray in it: if he is a sinner, that You forgive his sin; if he is poor, that You enrich him; if he is sick, that You heal him; if he is fearful, that You grant him safety; and I ask You not to turn Your gaze away from whoever enters it until he leaves it, except one who enters it with deviation or wrongdoing."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 15:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Certainly there was for Sheba⦆ Most of the people of tafsir (exegesis) hold that Saba' (Sheba) is the name of a man, and the tribe was named after him, just as Tamim is the name of a man and the tribe was named after him. Farwa ibn Musayk al-Ghutayfi narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Saba' is the name of a man who fathered ten sons. Six of them settled to the right (yamin, south), and four settled to the left (shām, north). As for the six who settled to the right: Himyar, Kindah, Madhhij, al-Azd, al-Ash'ar, and Anmar. As for the four who settled to the left: 'Amilah, Ghassan, Lakhm, and Judham." As for Saba', he was the son of Yashkhub ibn Ya'rub ibn Qahtan. It has also been said that Saba' is the name of a city, but the first view is the more correct.

His words: ﴿in their dwelling-places is a sign⦆. It was also read as "fi maskanihim" (in their dwelling-place, singular). The word āyah (sign) means a clear indication, and its meaning is: We made for them a sign that guides them to the realization that the blessings they possess are from Allah, exalted is He.

His words: ﴿two gardens, on the right and on the left⦆. In the narrative: they had a valley that flowed, and on the right of the valley were gardens arranged in rows, that is, orchards; likewise on the left of the valley.

His words: ﴿Eat of the provision of your Lord⦆, that is, We said to them: Eat of the provision of your Lord.

His words: ﴿and give thanks to Him⦆, that is, give thanks to Allah for His blessings.

His words: ﴿a good land⦆, that is, good in air, sweet in water, abundant in fruits. Ibn Zayd mentioned that there were no gnats, bedbugs, flies, scorpions, snakes, or anything of this kind in it, and a stranger who entered it with lice in his clothes would find the lice dying in his clothes because of the healthiness and goodness of the air.

His words: ﴿and a forgiving Lord⦆, that is, and a Lord who forgives sins if you give thanks for His blessings.

If it is said: What is the benefit of singling them out for this, since Allah forgives all His servants? The answer: The Lord's forgiveness together with the goodness of this land, to that degree, was granted only to them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 16:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But they turned away﴾, meaning: they turned away from giving thanks for the blessings.

And His saying: ﴿So We sent against them the flood of the al-'Arim﴾. The scholars differed concerning al-'Arim, giving four opinions. The first: it is the name of the valley. The second: it is the name of the dam (al-musannah), for they had built the dam with rock and bitumen between it and the water, and they placed on the dam gates that could be opened and closed; when they needed water they opened them, and when they had enough they closed them.

Al-Naqqash mentioned that this was the work of Bilqis, and that she had placed on the dam twelve outlets, from which twelve rivers flowed. The dam was a barrier between two mountains, and the waters behind the barrier gathered from the torrents. The third opinion: al-'Arim is the severe flood, meaning: We sent upon them the severe flood. The fourth opinion: al-'Arim is the name of the rat, that is, the mouse. It was also said: it was the name of the mole, and God Exalted empowered it over the dam until it bored through it, and the water entered and drowned the town and the gardens. Ibn al-A'rabi said: al-'Arim and al-Bar are names of the mouse, and from this is the saying of people: "So-and-so does not know a cat from a mouse" (la ya'rifu harran min barran), meaning: the tomcat (al-sinnawr) from the mouse. Abu al-Husayn ibn Faris mentioned in his exegesis that the people had heard that the destruction of their town would come by means of the mouse, from their soothsayers. So they brought cats and tied them at every embankment (in the dam), and a large red mouse came, attacked the cat, defeated it, entered the embankment, and the dam was undermined until it was pierced and broken through.

His saying: ﴿And We replaced their two gardens with two gardens bearing bitter fruit﴾, meaning: We replaced their two gardens, which had been bearing fruit, with two gardens bearing ﴿khamt﴾ (bitter produce). ﴿Khamt﴾ is read with tanwin on the lam (*ukulin khamtin*), and it was read without tanwin as an idafa (*ukli khamt*). The reading as an idafa is the clearer of the two readings in meaning, because al-khamt is the name of a tree that has thorns. Abu 'Ubayda said: every tree that has thorns is khamt if it bears no fruit. It was reported from some scholars that al-khamt is a tree bearing fruit called "the hyena's slough," which is not beneficial and dries up when ripe without benefiting anyone. The well-known opinion in tafsir, however, is that the fruit of al-khamt is al-barbar, and al-barbar is the fruit of the arak tree; so al-khamt is the arak, and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿the produce of khamt﴾. And al-akl (the produce) is the fruit.

As for the reading with tanwin, al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj said: every plant that has bitterness and astringency is khamt; on this basis, His saying ﴿khamt﴾ is an attribute of al-akl, and its meaning: bearing fruit of this description, namely bitterness and astringency.

His saying: ﴿and some tamarisk and a few lote trees﴾. The sidr is a well-known tree, and it is the lote tree (nabq). It was also said that this sidr was wild and not beneficial, whereas the sidr that is beneficial for washing the hand and other things is the one we know in gardens, and they did not have that.

That is, We repaid them for their disbelief with ingratitude (for the blessing).

And His words: ﴿And do We repay any but the ungrateful?﴾ It is said regarding punishment: "nujazi" (We repay), and regarding reward: "nujzi" (We reward). The meaning: Would such recompense be given except to one who denies the blessings? It is also said: "Would We be requited except the ungrateful?" That is: Would We call to account except the ungrateful? And it has been established by the narration of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever is subjected to a thorough reckoning will be punished." ʿĀʾisha said: "So I said: O Messenger of Allah, did not Allah the Exalted say: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to a easy account﴾?" He said: "That is merely the presentation (of deeds), but whoever is subjected to a thorough reckoning [of the account] will be punished."

If it is said: He has said, ﴿We replaced their two gardens with two gardens﴾, and the land in which there were tamarisk trees and lote-like thorny trees (al-khamt) is not called a garden? The answer to this: it is named so by way of contrast (al-muqabalah), like His words, Exalted is He: ﴿So whoever transgresses against you, transgress against him in the same way he transgressed against you﴾, and His words: ﴿And the recompense for an evil deed is an evil deed like it﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 18:

His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed visible towns﴾. The towns which We had blessed therein (are) al-Sham (Greater Syria). The meaning of "visible towns" is: connected (ith-mutta-silah). It was also said: "visible" means visible to the beholder, in the sense that when they stopped at one town they would see another town.

And His saying: ﴿And We measured out the travel therein﴾, meaning: We measured out their journeying between these towns. The meaning is: when they set out in the morning they would rest at midday in one town, and when they returned they would spend the night in one town. It was also said: the measuring of the journey means that their travel, in both the going and the returning, was according to the length of half a day, so when they had covered half a day they would reach a town with water and trees. Qatadah said: "They had no need to carry provisions." He also said: "A woman would place her basket on her head and pass under the trees, and the basket would be filled with fruit without her having to pick it."

And His saying: ﴿Travel therein by night and by day in security﴾, meaning: We said to them, "Travel therein by night and by day, safe from fear, hunger and thirst." The meaning of His saying "travel" is: We enabled them to travel. It is also said: the meaning of His saying "travel" is "they travel", an imperative in the sense of a declarative, and its meaning is: they travel therein by night and by day in security. And this is according to what we have mentioned.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they said: "Our Lord, make the distances between our journeys longer."﴾ It is also recited as "Ba'ada bayna asfarina" without the alif. Yahya ibn Ya'mur recited: "Rabbana ba'ada bayna asfarina" with a fatha on the ʿayn and the dāl. According to the well-known recitation (al-qira'a al-ma'ruf), the meaning of the verse is a supplication; according to the irregular recitation (al-qira'a al-shadhdha), the meaning of the verse is in the form of a statement. Mujahid said: they became insolent regarding the blessing and wearied of ease. Similarly, from Ibn ʿAbbas: they said, "Our Lord, make the distance between the towns long, so that we may ride the mounts and carry provisions through the deserts." This is like the saying of the Children of Israel: ﴿And when you said, "O Musa, we will not endure one kind of food"﴾ to the end of the verse. As for the irregular recitation, it is as if they found the nearby to be far, in the manner of the ignorant.

His saying: ﴿And they wronged themselves﴾, that is, by abandoning gratitude.

His saying: ﴿So We made them into tales and scattered them completely﴾, that is: tales for the generations that would come, and We divided and dispersed them into every kind of dispersal. Al-Sha'bi said: They scattered throughout the lands when their settlements were flooded and their gardens were destroyed. So the Azd went to Oman, Khuza'a went to Tihama, Ghassan went to al-Sham, the family of Khuzayma went to Iraq, and the Aws and the Khazraj went to Yathrib. The one among them who came to Madina was ʿAmr ibn ʿAmir, who is the grandfather of the Aws and the Khazraj.

In some tafsirs it is mentioned that their settlements numbered four thousand and seven hundred villages, connected from Saba' to al-Sham, village after village. Some of them said regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿We made them into tales﴾ that people use them as a proverb for tearing apart and scattering. The Arabs say: "The sons of so-and-so became the hands of Saba' and the hands of Saba'" when they scattered and dispersed. Al-Azhari recited:

(Ghaybā nura al-nāsa ilayhi tansaba ... min ṣādirin aw wāridin aydī Saba')

His saying: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for every steadfast, grateful person﴾, that is: steadfast upon trials, grateful for blessings.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 20:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And Iblis certainly found his assumption about them to be true﴾. It is recited "ṣaddaqa" (with light emphasis, i.e., taḫfīf). As for "ṣaddada" (with emphasis, tashdīd), its meaning is that he formed an assumption (ẓann) and it came true for him. His assumption is in the words of the Most High: ﴿Then I will surely come to them from before them and from behind them﴾, up to His words: ﴿and You will not find most of them grateful﴾. It is said that he assumed that if he led them astray, they would follow him, and so it was.

In the tafsir it is related that Iblis said: "I have expelled Adam from the Garden despite his great knowledge, and I have misled him. So I am more capable over his offspring."

As for the recitation with light emphasis, its meaning is: he was right about them in his assumption.

And His words: ﴿except a group of the believers﴾ mean: except all the believers. This is what most of the people of tafsir said, because the believers did not follow him in the fundamentals of religion. And Allah the Most High has said: ﴿Indeed, My servants, you have no authority over them﴾, meaning the believers. And it is related from some of them: "except a group of the believers" refers to the elite of the believers, those who obey Allah and do not disobey Him.

Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī said: "By Allah, he did not draw a sword against them, nor strike them with a whip. He only promised them and raised their hopes, and so they were deceived."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 21:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And he had no authority over them﴾, meaning: no authority over the believers.

And His words: ﴿except that We might know﴾, its meaning: so that We might know ﴿who believes in the Hereafter from who is in doubt about it﴾, meaning: that We might know the believer from the disbeliever with the knowledge of occurrence (ʿilm wuqūʿ). He already knows the unseen (ʿilm al-ghayb), and we have explained this before. Ibn Fāris said: this is in accordance with the manner of Arabic speech when addressing the ignorant. For if you say, "The knife cuts the meat," or "The meat cuts the knife," while it is known with certainty that the knife is what cuts the meat, the speech is nonetheless framed in address to the ignorant person and in making the matter clear to him.

And His words: ﴿And your Lord is Guardian over all things﴾, meaning: Watcher (raqīb).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 22:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Call upon those whom you claim besides Allah﴾ means: those whom you claim to be gods besides Allah. In the verse there is an ellipsis (hadhf), and what is omitted is: "call upon them so that they may remove from you the harm that has descended upon you." This was in the years of hunger, when Allah, exalted is He, struck them with hunger until they ate carrion, meaning the Quraysh. Then He said: ﴿They do not possess an atom's weight﴾, meaning: the idols do not possess an atom's weight, that is, the weight of a dhurrah (dhurra) of benefit or harm. The dhurrah is the red ant.

As for His saying: ﴿in the heavens or on the earth﴾, it is clear.

As for His saying: ﴿And they have no share therein⁠—﴾, meaning: the gods you call upon besides Allah have no partnership in the heavens and the earth.

As for His saying: ﴿And He has not from among them any helper﴾, meaning: any supporter (mu'in).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 23:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for one whom He has permitted﴾ — meaning: whom Allah has permitted. And it has been recited as "illa li-man udhina lahu" (except for the one for whom it has been permitted), meaning: except for the one for whom permission has been granted for his intercession.

And His saying: ﴿until, when terror is removed from their hearts﴾ — there must be an omitted element here, because "hatta" (until) by its nature requires connection to what precedes it, and nothing has been found that it connects to. So it is permissible that the omitted element is the affirmation of the terror of the angels and their fear when Allah, exalted is He, decrees a matter from the heaven to the earth.

And His saying: ﴿fuzzi'a 'an qulubihim﴾ (is removed from their hearts) means: the terror has been uncovered from their hearts.

And it has been recited in the irregular (shadh) reading: "fuzzi'a 'an qulubihim" (is removed from their hearts), meaning: their hearts have been emptied of fear.

It is established from the Prophet ﷺ, through the narration of Abu Hurayrah: "The angels hear the sound of the Revelation like the sound of a chain on smooth rock, so they swoon and strike their wings in submission to Allah, exalted is He."

And in another narration: "They fall prostrate upon their foreheads, and when the terror is removed from them, [they say: 'What has your Lord said?']" meaning: some of them said to others: "What has your Lord said?"

And His saying: ﴿they say: "The truth"﴾ means: they say, "Allah, exalted is He, has said the truth," meaning: the Revelation. As-Suddi and others mentioned that when the period of interruption (fatrah) between Jesus and Muhammad, peace be upon them both, lasted about six hundred years, the angels did not hear any revelation during this period. When Muhammad was sent, and [Allah said]: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?" Say: "Allah. And indeed, either we or you are upon guidance, or in manifest error."﴾, Gabriel descended with the Revelation, and they were terrified of it, fearing the establishment of the Hour. When the terror was removed from their hearts, they asked about what Allah had decreed of His command, and it was told to them that Allah, exalted is He, had revealed to Muhammad.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Most High, the Great﴾ means: the Exalted, the Magnificent in His attributes.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 24:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?"﴾ The provision from the heavens is the rain, and the provision from the earth is the plants.

His saying: ﴿Say: "Allah."﴾ That is: if they do not say, "Our provider is Allah, Exalted is He," then say to them, "Your provider is Allah, Exalted is He."

His saying: ﴿"And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error."﴾ If it is said: "'Aw" (or) in the speech of the Arabs is used for doubt, so how does the word "aw" fit in this place? And it is not permissible for anyone to doubt that he is upon guidance or upon error. The answer to this has several aspects. The first: what al-Farra' mentioned, namely that "aw" here means "wa" (and), and the alif is an added particle (silah), so it is as if he said: "And indeed we and you are upon guidance and in clear error," meaning: we are upon guidance and you are in error. Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said in verse:

(The lowest-born of the Banu Qushayr say, ... "Will you not forget 'Ali for all time?")

(I love Muhammad with a great love, and 'Abbas, and Hamzah, and the executor (al-Wasiyy)...)

(If their love is rectitude, I attain it, and in them is an example, if it is error...)

It was said: "You have not doubted." And he recited the saying of the Exalted: ﴿"And indeed we or you are surely upon guidance or in clear error."﴾ And this statement is related from 'Ikrimah.

The second answer: that His saying ﴿"And indeed we or you"﴾ came in the manner of intense certainty and in the manner of fairness in speech, like a man who says to another: "One of us is a liar, so is there any listener?" while he is certain that the truthful one is himself and the liar is his companion. Likewise a master says to his slave in intense anger: "Come, let us see which of us strikes his companion," while he knows that it is he who strikes his servant.

The third: what is related from Qatadah that he said regarding the meaning of the verse: we and you are not on one path; rather one of us is upon guidance and the other upon misguidance. Then the guided one of the two groups is known, and the misguided one of the two groups is known. This statement is close to the first, and it is good.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: You will not be asked about our sin﴾, meaning: about our sin.

And His saying: ﴿and we will not be asked about what you do﴾, meaning: about your deeds of disbelief and disobedience.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Our Lord will gather us together﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿Then He will judge between us﴾, meaning: He will decide between us. The Arabs call the judge a fattāḥ (one who opens, i.e., resolves matters), and we have mentioned this previously.

And His saying: ﴿And He is the Fattāḥ, the All-Knowing﴾ is clear. It is also said: He is the Judge, the One who knows the aspects of what is beneficial.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 27:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: Show me those whom you have joined with Him as partners.﴾ That is: those whom you have attached to Allah as partners.

And His saying: ﴿Show me﴾ means: inform me, what have they created? And what have they done?

And His saying: ﴿Nay﴾ means: if you do not answer with the truth, then say: "Nay," that is, the matter is not as you claim.

And His saying: ﴿Nay, rather, He is Allah, the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ That is: the Overpowering over His affair, the Wise in His management.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 34, verse 28:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind﴾, meaning: gathering them together by warning and conveying (the message). It was also said: ﴿And We have not sent you except to mankind comprehensively﴾, with inversion of the word order (taqdim wa ta'khir). And it has been established from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "I have been sent to the red and the black."

And on the authority of Ibn Zayd: "comprehensively to mankind" means restraining (kaffan) mankind from disbelief, and the ha' (in kaffah) is for emphasis (lil-mubalaghah).

As for His saying: ﴿bringing good tidings and warning﴾, meaning: giving good tidings and warning.

And His saying: ﴿but most of mankind do not know﴾, meaning: they do not know that you are a Prophet. And in some of the exegeses: the greatest benefit that Allah gives to His servants is knowledge and power, for by them a person acquires that which leads him to the pleasure of Allah, the Exalted. He said: Knowledge is more beneficial than power, because knowledge is purely beneficial, whereas power may be used to acquire disobedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 29:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ He means: the Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿Say: For you is an appointment of a Day from which you cannot delay by an hour, nor advance﴾. This has been explained as the Day of Resurrection, and it has also been explained as the Day of Death, and both are correct.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 31:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who disbelieve say: "We will never believe in this Qur'an, nor in what came before it."﴾ Meaning: they associated partners (with Allah) (ashraku).

And His words: ﴿nor in that which is before it﴾ meaning: of the Tawrah (Torah) and the Injil (Gospel).

And His words: ﴿If only you could see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord﴾ meaning: they are held back (mahbusun) before their Lord.

And His words: ﴿returning the word to one another﴾ meaning: some of them dispute with one another.

And His words: ﴿Those who were deemed weak will say to those who were arrogant﴾ meaning: they were looked down upon (istuhqiru), and they are the followers.

And His words: ﴿to those who were arrogant﴾ meaning: they acted tyrannically (tajabbaru), and they are the leaders and the nobles.

And His words: ﴿"Had it not been for you, we would have been believers!"﴾ meaning: had it not been that you were our leaders and chiefs, we would have believed in Allah and His Messenger.

The Almighty's words: ﴿Those who were arrogant said﴾, i.e., they acted arrogantly (takabbarū).

And His words: ﴿to those who were oppressed﴾, i.e., the followers (al-atbā').

And His words: ﴿Is it we who barred you from guidance after it had come to you?﴾, i.e., we prevented you.

And His words: ﴿Nay, but you were criminals﴾, i.e., the sin was yours in following your own desires.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 33:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "Rather, it was your scheming by night and day"﴾. That is: your scheming against us by night and day. The Arabs sometimes attribute the verb to "night and day" as a broadening of speech. The poet said:

(You blamed us, O Umm Ghaylan, for travelling by night, and you slept, though the night of the riding camels does not sleep.)

It was also said: "Rather, the scheming of night and day" means: long hope (tul al-amal), and long hope is the scheming of night and day in a figurative sense. In the irregular reading (shadhdh) it was recited: "Bal makru al-layli wa al-nahar", meaning: the alternation (kurur) of night and day.

His saying: ﴿when you commanded us to disbelieve in Allah and set up rivals to Him﴾, that is: equals (ashbah).

His saying: ﴿And they will conceal the regret﴾. We have already explained that the word ﴿asarru﴾ may mean "concealed" and may mean "displayed".

His saying: ﴿when they see the punishment﴾, that is: they witness it.

His saying: ﴿And We will put shackles around the necks of those who disbelieved﴾ is a branch of the punishment of the people of the Fire.

His saying: ﴿Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?﴾, that is: what they used to do of disbelief and sins.

Allah's saying: ﴿And We did not send a warner into any town but that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent."﴾ That is, its pampered ones and its wealthy ones; al-taraffuh (affluence) means blessing and comfort.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, we disbelieve in that with which you have been sent﴾ means: we deny it (jaahidun, those who reject and refuse to acknowledge it).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 35:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They said, "We have more wealth and children than you, and we will not be punished."﴾ That is: the affluent (al-mutrafun) said to the poor who had believed, "We have more wealth and children."

And His words: ﴿And we are not going to be punished﴾ — the punishment with which they are punished in this world, which is poverty. The second opinion, and it is the more apparent of the two opinions, is that the One who bestowed upon us and gave us wealth and children in this world will not punish us in the Hereafter.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it,﴾ and so on to the end of the verse. It was revealed to refute their saying. Its meaning: He extends provision as a test and trial, and restricts provision (as a means of looking after them).

As for His saying: ﴿but most of the people do not know﴾, it is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 37:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it is not your wealth nor your children that bring you near to Us in position﴾ — meaning: nearness (qurba). It is related from Tawus al-Yamani that he used to supplicate and say: "O Allah, keep wealth and children far from me, and grant me faith and righteous deeds."

And in the reports it is narrated that the Prophet said (ﷺ): "O Allah, whoever loves me, grant him contentment (al-'afaf) and sufficiency (al-kafaf); and whoever hates me, increase his wealth and his children."

As for His saying: ﴿except for one who has believed and done righteousness﴾, there are two opinions concerning it. The first: that this is an exception of a disconnected kind (istithna' munqati'), and its meaning is: "but [rather], whoever has believed and done righteousness."

The second opinion: the meaning of the verse is ﴿except for one who has believed and done righteousness﴾, so those — their wealth and their children bring them near to the obedience of Allah. This is the more evident of the two opinions.

As for His saying: ﴿For them is the reward of multiplication﴾, meaning: the multiplying (at-tad'if). It is said: the reward of multiplication (al-mudaʻafa), and multiplication is that He rewards one good deed with ten up to seven hundred.

As for His saying: ﴿and they will be in the upper chambers, secure﴾, meaning: (in) the chambers of Paradise, secure from punishment. It is said: from death. It is said: from griefs.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And those who strive against Our verses, trying to frustrate them﴾. We have already explained the meaning of ﴿معاجزين﴾ and ﴿معجزين﴾.

And His saying: ﴿those will be brought forth into the punishment﴾. That is, ﴿مدخلون﴾, meaning those who will be made to enter [it].

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 39:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord extends provision to whomever He wills of His servants and restricts it for him.﴾ If it is said: This is a repetition of the first verse, so there is no benefit in it? The answer to this: there is a benefit in it, which is that the first verse concerns one who does not know, since He said: ﴿But most of the people do not know﴾, and the second verse concerns one who knows the wisdom of Allah the Exalted in the extending and the restricting.

And His words: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it﴾, meaning: He will give its replacement. Scholars differed regarding the place where the replacement is given. The majority hold that it is in the Hereafter or in this world.

Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "There is not a morning but two angels call out. One of them says: 'O Allah, give the one who spends a replacement,' and the other says: 'O Allah, give the one who withholds a loss.'"

And from al-Hasan al-Basri, he said: It is in this world specifically, and if there were no replacement in this world, the servant would remain without provision. The first view is better.

And His words: ﴿And He is the best of those who provide sustenance﴾, meaning: the best of those who provide and give.

The Words of the Exalted: ﴿And on the Day He gathers them all together, He will say to the angels, "Did these people used to worship you?"﴾ God, exalted is He, says this to the angels as a rebuke to those who worshipped them. It is like His words, exalted is He: ﴿And when God says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides God'?"﴾ The meaning is as we have explained.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿They will say, "Glory be to You"﴾: the glorification (tasbih) of Allah is magnifying Him in a manner that negates from Him every imperfection.

And His saying: ﴿You are our Guardian, not them﴾: meaning, "We take You as our protector and do not take them as protectors."

And His saying: ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ (If it is said: how is His saying ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ correct, when they worshipped the angels?) The answer has two aspects. One of them: He said ﴿Rather, they used to worship the jinn﴾ because the jinn are those who made the worship of the angels appealing to them, (and what is meant by "the jinn" is the devils (shayatin)). The second view: they depicted the forms of the jinn and said, "These are the angels, so worship them."

And His saying: ﴿Most of them were believers in them﴾: its meaning is apparent."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 42:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So on that Day none of you will have power to benefit or harm another﴾, meaning: to bring about benefit and to repel harm.

And His saying: ﴿And We will say to those who did wrong, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."﴾, meaning: you used to reject.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 43:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when Our clear verses are recited to them﴾, meaning: manifest.

And His saying: ﴿They say, "This is none but a man who wants to turn you away from what your fathers used to worship"﴾, meaning: keep you from it, ﴿what your fathers used to worship﴾, meaning: of the idols.

And His saying: ﴿And they say, "This is nothing but a fabricated lie"﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is a lie, invented.

And His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved said of the truth when it came to them, "This is nothing but clear magic"﴾, meaning: evident.

Allah the Exalted's words: ﴿And We did not give them any books which they study﴾, meaning: which they read.

And His words: ﴿Nor did We send to them any warner before you﴾, meaning: no prophet came to the Arabs before you, and no book was sent down to them. By this is meant the Quraysh.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those before them denied,﴾ means: those who passed away before them, namely ʿAd, Thamud, the people of Musa, the people of Ibrahim, the people of Lut, and others.

And His saying: ﴿nor have they attained a tenth of what We gave them.﴾ Most of the people of tafsir (tafsir, exegesis of the Qur'an) hold that the meaning of the verse is that these disbelievers, namely the Quraysh, have not attained a tenth of what We gave those before them in strength, wealth and equipment. The second view is that the meaning is: those before them did not attain a tenth of what We gave these people; that is, the book of these people is the clearest of books, and their messenger is the best of messengers. The first view is the well-known one. As for al-maʿshar (ma'shar, a tenth), it is one tenth, and it was said: a tenth of a tenth, which is one part in a hundred; and it was said: it is a tenth of a tenth of a tenth, which is one part in a thousand.

His saying: ﴿So they denied My messengers, and how was My rejection?﴾ means: My denunciation and My change of their condition.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 46:

The words of His, the Exalted: ﴿Say: I only exhort you to one thing﴾. Mujahid said: "To obedience to Allah." It was also said: "To the Oneness of Allah (tawhid), which is His saying, 'There is no god but Allah' (la ilaha illa Allah)." Scholars of the meanings of the Qur'an (ahl al-ma'ani), such as al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj and others, mentioned that the meaning of His saying, ﴿I exhort you to one thing﴾, is: I command you with one single quality. Then He explained the quality, saying: ﴿that you stand up for Allah, in pairs and individually﴾, meaning: you gather together and reflect and discuss, and you withdraw alone and ponder. The meaning is: look into the condition of Muhammad (ﷺ) both when in company and when alone, so that you will know that he is not a sorcerer, nor a soothsayer, nor is there madness in him, nor is what he brings poetry.

As for His saying, ﴿stand up for Allah﴾, the exegetes said: it does not mean the standing that is the opposite of sitting; rather, it is like His, the Exalted, saying: ﴿and that you stand up for orphans with justice﴾.

As for His saying, ﴿then you reflect: there is no madness in your companion﴾, meaning: there is no jinn-possession (madness) in him.

As for His saying, ﴿He is only a warner to you before a severe punishment﴾, meaning: a great one.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Whatever reward I have asked of you, it is yours﴾, i.e., whoever receives it, it is yours, meaning: I have left it to you. The meaning is: I have not asked you for any recompense, not that he asked and then left it.

And His saying: ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, i.e., my recompense is only from Allah.

And His saying: ﴿And He is, over all things, Witness﴾, i.e., Witness.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Say: Indeed, my Lord casts down the truth.﴾ That is: He brings the truth.

And His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen.﴾ It is in the accusative (manṣūb) by virtue of inna (ʾinna, "indeed"), and it was recited as "ʿAllāmu al-ghuyūb" in the nominative (marfūʿ), meaning: He is the Knower of the unseen.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 49:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Say: The truth has come﴾ means: the Qur'an. It is also said: the Messenger.

And His words: ﴿And falsehood neither originates nor restores﴾. Qatadah said: "The falsehood here is Satan," meaning: Satan originates nothing [﴿and neither restores﴾].

There is another view regarding the verse, namely that Allah the Most High casts the truth against falsehood, so falsehood perishes and nothing of it remains that could originate anything or restore it. It is also said: the falsehood is the idols.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 50:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Say, "If I go astray, I only go astray to my own detriment."﴾ The exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sent and began to criticise the idols, the polytheists said to him, "You have indeed gone astray by abandoning the religion of your forefathers." So Allah the Exalted revealed this verse.

His words, ﴿I only go astray to my own detriment﴾ mean: the burden of my going astray falls upon me.

His words, ﴿And if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me﴾ mean: by the Qur'an and the proofs.

His words, ﴿Indeed, He is Hearing, Near﴾ are clear in meaning.

"The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you could see when they are seized with terror﴾ means: and if you could see when they are seized with terror at the time of being resurrected. In the verse there is an omitted response (jawab), and the omitted part is: and if you could see when they are seized with terror at the time of being resurrected, you would witness a lesson by which one takes heed. It is also said: ﴿And if you could see when they are seized with terror﴾ means the time of death.

And His saying: ﴿Then there is no escape﴾ means: they will not escape from Allah, as Allah says in another place: ﴿But it is no longer time for escape﴾.

And His saying: ﴿And they will be seized from a near place﴾ — in the exegesis: they will be seized from beneath their feet. It is also said: they will be seized from the belly of the earth (to its surface)."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 52:

His saying: ﴿And they will say, "We believe in Him."﴾ That is, on the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: at the time of death. This is in the sense of His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when they saw Our might, they said, "We believe in Allah alone."﴾

As for His saying: ﴿And how can they reach [the faith] from a distant place?﴾ Mujahid, Qatadah and many of the exegetes said: al-tanawush (the reaching out, grasping) is al-tanawul (taking hold of something). The poet said:

(And she [the camel] reaches for the trough, reaching up from above,
a reaching by which she cuts across the wide deserts.)

The meaning of the verse according to this is that they wish to grasp faith, but it has become far from them and eluded them, so how can they obtain it?

It was also read as "wa-anna lahumu al-tanawush" with a hamza (al-tanaush). The lexicographers mention that al-nane'sh (the verb being a variant) is movement with slowness, so the meaning according to this is: from where for them is their movement toward that for which they have no means?

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: the meaning of His saying, ﴿And how can they reach [the faith]?﴾ is that they ask for a return to the world, and how can they have a return?

As for His saying: ﴿from a distant place﴾, that is: from the Hereafter to the world.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 53:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they had disbelieved in it before﴾, meaning: in the Quran. It is also said: in Muhammad.

And His saying: ﴿before﴾, meaning: in this world.

And His saying: ﴿and they cast [assumptions] about the unseen﴾, meaning: they conjecture guesses about the unseen. The meaning of conjecturing about the unseen is that they say what they do not know. Their saying about what they do not know is that they said: "Muhammad is a sorcerer, a liar, a soothsayer, and a poet." It is also said: their saying about what they do not know is that they say: "There is no resurrection and no Paradise" and no Fire.

.

And His saying: ﴿from a far-off place﴾: they say, "How far-fetched is this!" It is also said: from a far-off place, meaning: far from their knowledge. Al-qadhf is throwing and casting, and the overall meaning is that they plunge into what they have no knowledge of.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 34, verse 54:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire﴾. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: It is faith and the acceptance of repentance. It is also said: wealth and children. (It is said as well:) the blessings of this world and its splendor. And it is related from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that he said: "I never recited this verse without thinking of cold water."

His saying: ﴿As was done with their counterparts before﴾, meaning: the past nations. It is also said: the companions of the Elephant. Al-ashya' (the counterparts) is the plural of shi'ah, and they are the sects.

His saying: ﴿Indeed they were in disquieting doubt﴾, meaning: they were in doubt, doubting. In this verse there is evidence that the doubter is a disbeliever, contrary to what some people have said, and that is a grave error in religion. This verse indicates that the doubter is a disbeliever and is in the Fire, and the same is indicated by the saying of Exalted God: ﴿And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in vain. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire﴾. He has made disbelief and the Fire obligatory for them on account of mere assumption. It has been related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning the saying of Exalted God: ﴿And they say, "We have believed in it." But how could they attain it from a place so distant?﴾ that he said: this verse was revealed concerning the army of al-Sufyani, a man [who will emerge] among his maternal relatives from the tribe of Kalb. God will cause them to be swallowed up in al-Bayda', except for one man who will inform the people of what God did to them. And there is a story concerning this.
